title: Cross-tenant delegated key custody and private-deploy security acceptance checklist
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Scoped PRD and acceptance checklist for enabling delegated key custody (BYOK and Redwood-escrowed options) across multiple customer tenants in private/VPC deployments. This ticket covers requirements clarification, scope decisions, and the formal acceptance criteria for SSO/SAML, RBAC role mapping, immutable audit logging, and KMS/HSM integration. It is focused on cross-tenant administrative delegation scenarios (e.g., MSPs and consultants acting on behalf of customers) where key custody or temporary key escrow is requested. The goal is to provide a clear, testable sign-off path so Delivery and Security can validate compliance controls before GA rollout.
acceptance_criteria: SSO: SAML 2.0 authentication supported for private consoles with both IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows validated against customer IdPs using test metadata.
Provisioning: SCIM-based user/group provisioning for RBAC sync is implemented and demonstrably syncs role mappings within 5 minutes for sample orgs.
MFA: Account policy enforcement supports customer-enforced MFA via their IdP; test accounts must require MFA during sign-in for all elevated role tests.
RBAC: Role matrix defined for tenant-admin, delegated-admin, auditor, operator, and read-only roles with least-privilege checks captured as unit tests and integration tests.
Delegated custody flows: Two delegation modes implemented and tested: time-bound delegated key escrow (customer-approved) and MSP-permissioned operations without permanent key transfer.
KMS/HSM: Customer BYOK accepted via import or HSM-backed key generation; HSM attestation logs stored and verifiable; keys marked with origin metadata in audit logs.
Key lifecycle: Rotation, revocation, and emergency key-swap performed without >5s median request latency degradation for active connections; documented rollback steps exist.
Audit logs: Immutable audit trail for all custody changes, RBAC grants/revocations, and key operations; logs preserved for 365 days and exportable to customer SIEM (via syslog/S3 connector).
Encryption/standards: All KMS/HSM operations meet FIPS 140-2 Level 3 (or equivalent) attestations and TLS 1.2+ for transport; evidence attached.
E2E demos: Deliver two runbooks and recorded demos showing onboarding, delegation approval, key rotation, and recovery that security and a sample customer review and accept.
Automated tests: CI tests for RBAC enforcement and custody auditability are present in the repository and pass on PRs before release.
Documentation: Confluence PRD, customer-runbook, and support escalation playbook published and linked before sign-off.
Legal & Compliance: Legal review confirms data residency and key escrow terms for target regions and signs off on escrow contract template.
Performance: Baseline performance dashboards show no >10% P95 latency regression for inference paths when delegation features are enabled under expected load profile.
decisions: Opted for explicit two-mode delegation (temporary escrow vs permissioned MSP operations) to avoid permanent cross-tenant key transfers.
Require IdP MFA enforcement for any account granted delegated-admin or higher to reduce risk of credential compromise.
Audit trail will be write-once S3 object store with signed manifests rather than append-only DB to simplify retention and export obligations.
HSM integration to be supported via vendor-agnostic PKCS#11 interface, with vendors certified on an approve list to meet FIPS requirements.
Customer BYOK import will accept wrapped keys with attestation metadata; Redwood will not store customer key plaintext at rest in hosted components.
tradeoffs: Usability vs security: Time-bound escrow requires customer approval UX which adds 1-2 extra steps during onboarding but reduces long-term exposure risk.
Complexity vs speed: Supporting multiple HSM vendors increases QA burden and delivery time; initial launch will ship with two validated vendors and expand later.
Operational cost: Immutable long-term retention of audit logs increases storage costs; retention policy set to 365 days by default with paid extensions later.
Performance impact: Enforcing synchronous attestation checks on every key operation increases tail latency; switched to async attestation verification with gating on policy breach.
